title: Warships Fired Cannonballs Chained Together #shorts

lines.text: Old sailing warships didn't just fire cannonballs. Sometimes they fired two balls chained together, spinning like giant nunchucks.
Picture a captain chasing an enemy ship. He doesn't want to sink it. He wants to steal it.
So he yells, "Load the chain shot!"
The balls fly out, the chain whips open, and it shreds the enemy's sails and ropes like a giant weed whacker.
Now the enemy ship can't move, and the captain just sails over and takes it.
But forts on land had something worse. They baked cannonballs in a furnace until they glowed red hot.
The new gunner asks, "Uh, won't a red hot ball set off the gunpowder?"
The old gunner says, "That's why we pack in wet clay first."
You see, wooden ships were basically floating piles of firewood, painted in tar.
One glowing ball gets stuck in the wood, and the ship starts burning from the inside.
It's like tossing one hot coal into a haystack. You don't need a big hit. Just one that sticks.
Sailors even had a saying: a ship's a fool to fight a fort.
Because ships fight with cannons, and forts fight with ovens.

sources: https://www.navy.mil (Nelson: 'a ship's a fool to fight a fort')
